item.text:
This turn closed the last documented quiesce gap and turned a flaky attempt into a clean result.

**Membership change while quiesced (new coverage, passes)**

A dedicated three-node test (`TestAuditMembershipChangeAfterQuiesce`) idles the cluster into quiesce, then deletes a follower. The leader logs `exited from quiesce, msg type ConfigChangeEvent`, the removal is applied, and a subsequent proposal commits. That confirms the config-change path wakes the cluster the way `handleReadIndex` does — and, by contrast, sharpens F13's scope: only proposals were missing the `qs.record` call.

While building it I hit two of my own test bugs before the product was ever implicated — deleting node 2 when node 2 happened to be the leader (`raft cluster already closed`), and an election-overlap flake in the earlier quiesce test. Both were fixed in the test, and neither was reported as a defect.

**Report state**

- F13 section now covers idle reads, proposals, user-requested snapshots, membership changes and leader loss under quiesce.
- Inventory lists both quiesce test files; "Unresolved work" narrows to observer/witness nodes in quiesce mode.
- Matrix updated to 42 audit tests (27 passing, 15 deliberate repro failures), root package at 24 tests; command log includes the new runs.
- All three quiesce tests pass together on the fixed copy (11.3 s), and the repro test files are synced into `audit/diag-fixes/`.

The audited implementation remains byte-identical to `../source`; everything added is build-tagged tests, harnesses, logs and report text.
